== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/tagged.rs#L1-L20
     1  //! con-leche: none — the tagged counted handle of DESIGN.md §3.2 (task #94).
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::tagged` — **the crate's only `unsafe`, and it does not know what an
     4  //! `Expr` is**.
     5  //!
     6  //! One counted handle, one word wide, whose low four bits say which of a
     7  //! *scheme's* node types the rest of it points at.  Every block is allocated
     8  //! 16-aligned, which is what frees those four bits; sixteen kinds fit, and
     9  //! each kind's block is as wide as that kind needs rather than as wide as the
    10  //! widest.  That is the whole idea, and the measurement behind it is task
    11  //! #94's report: `Expr`'s nodes go from a flat 64-byte block to 32 or 48
    12  //! bytes, which is −45 % of Mathlib's peak.
    13  //!
    14  //! **This module is generic.**  It names no term type, no constructor and no
    15  //! kind: a *scheme* is a table, and [`tagged_kinds!`] turns it into the
    16  //! tag→type dispatch and the release.  `ron::node` is the one instantiation
    17  //! today (`Expr`'s ten blocks); `Name`, `Level` and `PropWhen` keep
    18  //! `ron::ptr::P` (DESIGN.md §3.2 — their nodes are not the bulk, and a
    19  //! uniform block costs them nothing).
    20  //!

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L130-L254
   130  const USAGE: &str = "\
   131  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
   132                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
   133                 FILE.ndjson
   134         con-ron --help
   135  
   136    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   137                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   138                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists,
   139                      ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean), so a stream declaring a
   140                      theorem of type False is never accepted
   141                      (ConLeche.no_False_theorem_accepted).  What the port
   142                      proves is that same statement about THIS program's
   143                      pipeline, from the file's bytes to the fold
   144                      (conron.no_False_declaration, OVERVIEW.md section 3).
   145    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   146                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   147                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   148    --jobs=<n>        the check phase's worker count: <n> workers claim records
   149                      one at a time off a shared counter, and --jobs=1 runs the
   150                      plain loop with no counter and no result table.  The
   151                      verdict, and the declaration a rejection names, are the
   152                      same at every <n>: the results are walked in RECORD order,
   153                      so the first failing record in fold order is the one
   154                      reported.  Each worker reserves 1 GiB of address space for
   155                      its stack, so a run under `ulimit -v` needs 3x the
   156                      checker's resident set plus a gigabyte per worker; the
   157                      DEFAULT is one worker per hardware thread capped at 16 for
   158                      that reason (con-leche's uncapped default aborts on a
   159                      96-thread machine).  0 or a non-numeral is a usage error,
   160                      as in con-leche.
   161    --no-mark-persistent
   162                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP: the mark it turns off is a
   163                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   164                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this program's counts are
   165                      std::sync::Arc counts -- atomic by type, in every lane,
   166                      with no runtime mark to clear.  A run that passes it says
   167                      so on stderr.
   168    --progress[=<stride>]
   169                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   170                      phase:
   171                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   172                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   173                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> checks pending t=<s>s
   174                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   175                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   176                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s, <n> workers
   177                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   178                      declaration is installed (<i> is its FOLD position, which
   179                      the stream's record index sits near but not at a fixed
   180                      offset above), so a run that dies in the install phase
   181                      names the declaration it died in on its last line.  A
   182                      check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th COMPLETED
   183                      check.  On a failure the phase's closing line says so
   184                      ('install failed at', 'check failed at') and the summary
   185                      still prints.  Bare --progress is stride 1; a stride that
   186                      is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is a usage error.
   187    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   188                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   189                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.
   190    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   191                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   192                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   193                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   194                      verified core and decoded by it.
   195    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   196                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   197                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   198                      measurement can be reproduced.
   199  
   200  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   201  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   202  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   203  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   204  The mimalloc one is `con_ron_dump::MiMallocTight`, which enters mimalloc by
   205  `mi_malloc` rather than `mi_malloc_aligned` for word-aligned requests: -4.5 %
   206  instructions and -7.4 % wall against the `mimalloc` crate's own entry (task
   207  #92), and one size class back for anything 42 to 48 bytes wide.
   208  
   209  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   210  exits 3 without reading its input.
   211  
   212  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   213  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: con-leche's exit 1 for it is the Lean
   214  runtime's own panic, and this program instead aborts the way Rust aborts on a
   215  failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT, which a
   216  shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   217  
   218  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   219  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   220  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   221  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   222  declaration IS counted -- the preparation moves it to the front rather than
   223  dropping it, and it is what installs.  That count is a property of the INPUT.
   224  The number of environment CONSTANTS is not: an inductive record installs
   225  several constants (type former, constructors, recursor, projection table), so
   226  it moves when the representation moves.
   227  
   228  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   229  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   230  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   231  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   232  the export chose.  The stream's OWN copy of a prelude declaration is moved to
   233  the front in the prelude's order, and only the prelude records the stream does
   234  not declare are synthesised; a pinned operation's stream-certified structural
   235  ground (Nat.ble, Nat.sub, Nat.mul) is HOISTED ahead of the operation when the
   236  stream declares it later.  All of that is one pure total function from the
   237  file's records to the fold's input (con_ron::frontend::prepare); the parse
   238  itself only decodes, and recognising a block as a pinned basis block or a
   239  record as the quotient package's is the FOLD's.
   240  
   241  environment (con-leche's):
   242    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   243                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   244                                 declines it, having found no route
   245    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   246                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   247    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   248  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches and they go with it: no
   249  environment variable this program reads can shape a verdict, which is
   250  con-leche's own rule -- every such switch is a command-line flag.
   251  
   252  NOT PORTED: CON_LECHE_INMODEL_DUMP, the debug splice of the generated records
   253  into a copy of the input -- it is written through con-leche's annotated-NDJSON
   254  writer (`Frontend/ExportWrite.lean`), an output path this checker does not

    42  //! |---|---|---|

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/node.rs#L1-L14
     1  //! con-leche: none — `Expr`'s instantiation of `ron::tagged` (DESIGN.md §3.2, task #94).
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::node` — **the ten `Expr` cells, as a table**.
     4  //!
     5  //! Until task #94 every `Expr` node was a `P<ExprNode>`: a block as wide as
     6  //! the *widest* `ExprKind` arm, plus a kind word, plus `Arc`'s two counts —
     7  //! 64 bytes for an `app`, which is 65 % of the live nodes of a real term
     8  //! (task #88's census) and needs 32.  Lean's own representation does not do
     9  //! that: the kind is in the object header, and each constructor's object is
    10  //! as wide as its own fields.
    11  //!
    12  //! So the kind moved into the handle, and `ron::tagged` is the machinery that
    13  //! puts it there.  **This file has no `unsafe` in it** — it is a table of ten
    14  //! `tag => variant: type` lines, ten struct declarations, and thin wrappers:

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/ptr.rs#L1-L8

     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::ptr` — **the one place the core names its shared pointer**
     4  //! (DESIGN.md §3.2, task #44).
     5  //!
     6  //! con-leche's terms are persistent trees with sharing, which the port gives
     7  //! reference counting: `P<T>` is the handle, and the model erases it
     8  //! (`Arc T := T`, plus four definitions).  Which *concrete* counted pointer

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/expr.rs#L479-L495
   479  pub fn app(f: Expr, a: Expr) -> Expr {
   480      let df: u64 = data(&f);
   481      let da: u64 = data(&a);
   482      let h: u64 = hash32(name::mix_hash(
   483          17,
   484          name::mix_hash(hash_of_data(df), hash_of_data(da)),
   485      ));
   486      let d: u64 = pack_data(
   487          h,
   488          max_u64(bvar_of_data(df), bvar_of_data(da)),
   489          max_u64(fvar_of_data(df), fvar_of_data(da)),
   490          lp_of_data(df) || lp_of_data(da),
   491      );
   492      node::alloc_app(d, f, a)
   493  }

  5086  pub fn whnf_core(
  5087      mode: &CheckMode,
  5088      fuel: u64,
  5089      st: &mut CState,
  5090      fe: &FEnv,
  5091      d: u64,
  5092      e: &Expr,
  5093  ) -> CheckM<Expr> {
  5094      const M: [u32; 24] = [
  5095          102, 117, 101, 108, 32, 101, 120, 104, 97, 117, 115, 116, 101, 100, 58, 32, 119, 104,
  5096          110, 102, 67, 111, 114, 101,
  5097      ];
  5098      if fuel == 0 {
  5099          Err(core_types::internal(core_types::code_points(&M)))
  5100      } else {
  5101          match whnf_core_probe(st, e) {
  5102              Some(r) => Ok(r),
  5103              None => match whnf_core_body_i(mode, fuel - 1, st, fe, d, e) {
  5104                  Err(err) => Err(err),
  5105                  Ok(r) => {
  5106                      st.whnf_core_c.insert(expr::dup(e), expr::dup(&r));
  5107                      Ok(r)
  5108                  }
  5109              },
  5110          }
  5111      }
  5112  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/checker_c.rs#L123-L132
   123  pub fn or_else_step(attempt: CheckM<bool>) -> OrElseStep {
   124      match attempt {
   125          Ok(true) => OrElseStep::Matched,
   126          Ok(false) => OrElseStep::Continue,
   127          Err(e) => match e {
   128              CheckError::Native(m) => OrElseStep::Failed(CheckError::Native(m)),
   129              _ => OrElseStep::Recovered(e),
   130          },
   131      }
   132  }

== crates/con-ron-dump/src/lib.rs#L155-L203
   155  pub struct MiMallocTight;
   156  
   157  #[cfg(all(feature = "mimalloc", not(feature = "jemalloc")))]
   158  unsafe impl std::alloc::GlobalAlloc for MiMallocTight {
   159      #[inline]
   160      unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: std::alloc::Layout) -> *mut u8 {
   161          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   162              libmimalloc_sys::mi_malloc(layout.size()) as *mut u8
   163          } else {
   164              libmimalloc_sys::mi_malloc_aligned(layout.size(), layout.align()) as *mut u8
   165          }
   166      }
   167  
   168      #[inline]
   169      unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: std::alloc::Layout) -> *mut u8 {
   170          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   171              libmimalloc_sys::mi_zalloc(layout.size()) as *mut u8
   172          } else {
   173              libmimalloc_sys::mi_zalloc_aligned(layout.size(), layout.align()) as *mut u8
   174          }
   175      }
   176  
   177      #[inline]
   178      unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, _layout: std::alloc::Layout) {
   179          libmimalloc_sys::mi_free(ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void);
   180      }
   181  
   182      #[inline]
   183      unsafe fn realloc(
   184          &self,
   185          ptr: *mut u8,
   186          layout: std::alloc::Layout,
   187          new_size: usize,
   188      ) -> *mut u8 {
   189          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   190              libmimalloc_sys::mi_realloc(ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void, new_size) as *mut u8
   191          } else {
   192              libmimalloc_sys::mi_realloc_aligned(
   193                  ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void,
   194                  new_size,
   195                  layout.align(),
   196              ) as *mut u8
   197          }
   198      }
   199  }
   200  
   201  #[cfg(all(feature = "mimalloc", not(feature = "jemalloc")))]
   202  #[global_allocator]
   203  static GLOBAL_ALLOC: MiMallocTight = MiMallocTight;

   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv

   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/node.rs#L228-L263
   228  pub fn view(e: &Expr) -> ExprView<'_> {
   229      match e.0.tag() {
   230          TAG_BVAR => ExprView::Bvar(&e.0.cast::<NodeBvar>().i),
   231          TAG_FVAR => {
   232              let c: &NodeFvar = e.0.cast::<NodeFvar>();
   233              ExprView::Fvar(&c.idx, &c.ty)
   234          }
   235          TAG_SORT => ExprView::Sort(&e.0.cast::<NodeSort>().u),
   236          TAG_CONST => {
   237              let c: &NodeConst = e.0.cast::<NodeConst>();
   238              ExprView::Const(&c.n, &c.us)
   239          }
   240          TAG_APP => {
   241              let c: &NodeApp = e.0.cast::<NodeApp>();
   242              ExprView::App(&c.f, &c.a)
   243          }
   244          TAG_LAM => {
   245              let c: &NodeLam = e.0.cast::<NodeLam>();
   246              ExprView::Lam(&c.ty, &c.body, &c.m)
   247          }
   248          TAG_FORALL_E => {
   249              let c: &NodeForallE = e.0.cast::<NodeForallE>();
   250              ExprView::ForallE(&c.ty, &c.body, &c.m)
   251          }
   252          TAG_LET_E => {
   253              let c: &NodeLetE = e.0.cast::<NodeLetE>();
   254              ExprView::LetE(&c.ty, &c.value, &c.body)
   255          }
   256          TAG_LIT => ExprView::Lit(&e.0.cast::<NodeLit>().l),
   257          TAG_PROJ => {
   258              let c: &NodeProj = e.0.cast::<NodeProj>();
   259              ExprView::Proj(&c.n, &c.idx, &c.e)
   260          }
   261          t => crate::ron::tagged::bad_tag(t),
   262      }
   263  }

== crates/con-ron/src/in_model/mod.rs#L12-L16
    12  //! Soundness needs nothing from this module: a wrong record is rejected or
    13  //! declined by the fold, never accepted.  Its correctness decides only
    14  //! *coverage* — which blocks accept — and every decline names its class, so
    15  //! the residual is exact and positive.  Nothing here is verified, and nothing
    16  //! here is in §3.4's Aeneas subset.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L21-L27
    21  //! `check_decls_driver` is `installed::check_decls`' body with the phase
    22  //! boundary visible (`Main.lean:318-421 checkDeclsIO`): phase A installs every
    23  //! record with `annot_decl_step`, phase B checks every recorded declaration
    24  //! from a fresh `CState` with `check_pending`.  It is step for step the fold
    25  //! `ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:438-455 checkDecls` — which is why an
    26  //! observer that prints between the steps changes no verdict, and why ONE
    27  //! loop serves the plain run and the `--progress` heartbeat alike.

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L15-L21
    15  //! **The verdict, and the record a rejection names, are the same at every
    16  //! `--jobs`.**  A worker's result is the record's index with its outcome; the
    17  //! workers' arrays are merged *by record index* into one table and the table is
    18  //! walked in **record order**, stopping at the first failing record in fold
    19  //! order.  That walk is `check_pending_list`'s, whatever the workers' timing,
    20  //! so the pool cannot report the second failure of a stream that has two —
    21  //! `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2, 3, 4
